record.paper_title: Spectral analysis for a class of integral-difference operators: known facts, new results, and open problems
record.original_question: Consider the Gaussian equilibrium distribution case in which the truncated restricted operator K_phi^a acts on functions on [-a,a] by (K_phi^a u)(x) = integral from -a to a of (u(x) phi(s) - u(s) phi(x)) / |x - s| ds, with phi(x) = C exp(-x^2), and is equivalently rescaled to an operator K_a on [-1,1] with phi_a(x) = C_a exp(-a^2 x^2). Suppose the established asymptotic result is that, for every M > 0, the dimension of the spectral subspace E_a[-M,M] H_a tends to infinity as a tends to infinity, so zero is a spectral concentration point for the limit operator. Do the discrete spectra of these truncated operators condense into continuous spectrum as a tends to infinity, and what are the other spectral properties of the limit operator?

evidence.quote: we study a family of operators Kϕa : u(x) −→ ∫a−a (u(x)ϕ(s) − u(s)ϕ(x))/|x − s| ds on the interval [−a,a]
Ka : u(x) −→ ∫1−1 (u(x)ϕa (s) − u(s)ϕa (x))/|x − s| ds on the interval [−1,1], where ϕa (x) := Ca e−a2x2.
For any M > 0, dim Ea [−M,M]Ᏼa −→ ∞ as a −→ ∞.

Other spectral properties of the limit operator are still unknown. In particular, it would be very interesting to clarify if the discrete spectrum of the truncated operators condenses into continuous one when a → ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each a > 0, let H_a = L^2([-a, a]) and consider the integral-difference operator K_φ^a acting on suitable functions u on [-a, a] by
  (K_φ^a u)(x) = ∫_{-a}^{a} (u(x) φ(s) − u(s) φ(x)) / |x − s| ds,
where φ(x) = C e^{−x^2} and C > 0 is a fixed normalization constant (e.g. so that ∫_{-∞}^{∞} φ = 1). By the rescaling x = a y, this operator is unitarily equivalent to an operator K_a on L^2([-1, 1]) defined by
  (K_a u)(x) = ∫_{-1}^{1} (u(x) φ_a(s) − u(s) φ_a(x)) / |x − s| ds,
with φ_a(x) = C_a e^{−a^2 x^2} (C_a chosen analogously). Each K_a is self-adjoint and nonnegative; let E_a(·) denote its spectral projection. It is known that for every M > 0,
  dim E_a([−M, M]) H_a → ∞ as a → ∞,
so that 0 is a point of spectral concentration in the large-a limit.

Question: As a → ∞, does the discrete spectrum of the family {K_a} condense into continuous spectrum of a limiting operator? More generally, determine the spectral properties (nature of the spectrum: pure point, absolutely continuous, singular continuous; multiplicity; spectral measure) of the limit operator obtained from K_a as a → ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: A search for the spectral analysis of this family of integral-difference operators with Gaussian equilibrium turns up the related work on spectral analysis of integral-difference collision operators (e.g. by Melnikov and collaborators), but no source establishes the condensation of the discrete spectrum into a continuous one for the Gaussian truncation, nor a complete description of the limit operator's spectral properties. The question is explicitly stated as not yet resolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: On Spectral Analysis of an Integral-Difference Operator
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral analysis of integral-difference collision operators with eigenfunctions of discrete and continuous spectrum constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature exists on spectral analysis of such integral-difference operators, but the specific limit-spectrum question for the Gaussian truncated family is not resolved there.
